title.en: Suankularb M.1 English (GATE and English Program) — Practice paper 3
title.th: ภาษาอังกฤษ สอบเข้า ม.1 สวนกุหลาบ (GATE และ EP) — ชุดที่ 3

note.en: 60 questions in 60 minutes, six parts: conversation, vocabulary, grammar, error identification, cloze and reading. GATE and English Program applicants take the same paper; EP applicants need a higher score. DeepDistrict practice format based on tutor summaries — not an official or past paper.
note.th: 60 ข้อ 60 นาที 6 ตอน: บทสนทนา คำศัพท์ ไวยากรณ์ หาจุดผิด เติมคำในบทความ และการอ่าน ผู้สมัคร GATE และ EP ใช้ข้อสอบชุดเดียวกัน ผู้สมัคร EP ต้องได้คะแนนสูงกว่า — แบบฝึกของ DeepDistrict ตามข้อมูลจากสถาบันกวดวิชา ไม่ใช่ข้อสอบจริงหรือข้อสอบเก่า

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอบคุณ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "Thank you so much for helping me carry these boxes."
B: "______"
choices: It was no trouble at all.

explanation.en: "It was no trouble at all." is a polite reply to thanks. "Thanks a lot." would be thanking A back, which makes no sense, and the other two replies do not answer thanks.
explanation.th: "It was no trouble at all." (ไม่ลำบากเลย) ใช้ตอบรับคำขอบคุณอย่างสุภาพ ส่วน "Thanks a lot." เป็นการขอบคุณกลับซึ่งไม่สมเหตุสมผล และอีกสองคำตอบไม่ได้ตอบคำขอบคุณ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Telephone language: offering to take a message
skill.th: ภาษาโทรศัพท์: การเสนอรับฝากข้อความ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "Hello, may I speak to Khun Wichai, please?"
B: "I'm afraid he's in a meeting at the moment. ______"

explanation.en: When the person is not available, the polite offer is "Can I take a message?" "Who are you?" is too direct and rude on the phone, and "Please call me back." makes no sense because B is not the person A wants.
explanation.th: เมื่อคนที่ต้องการคุยด้วยไม่ว่าง ควรเสนออย่างสุภาพว่า "Can I take a message?" (ฝากข้อความไว้ไหมคะ) ส่วน "Who are you?" ห้วนและไม่สุภาพ และ "Please call me back." ไม่สมเหตุสมผลเพราะ B ไม่ใช่คนที่ A ต้องการคุยด้วย

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การให้คำแนะนำ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "I've got a terrible headache."
B: "______"
choices: Why don't you lie down for a while?

explanation.en: "Why don't you …?" is a friendly way to give advice. "I'm glad to hear that." is for good news, "What a nice surprise!" for a happy surprise, and "Don't mention it." answers thanks.
explanation.th: "Why don't you …?" ใช้แนะนำอย่างเป็นมิตร ส่วน "I'm glad to hear that." ใช้กับข่าวดี "What a nice surprise!" ใช้เมื่อประหลาดใจในทางดี และ "Don't mention it." ใช้ตอบคำขอบคุณ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอร้องอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "Would you mind turning the music down a little? I'm trying to study."
B: "______"
choices: Not at all. I'll turn it up.
Oh, sorry! I didn't realise it was so loud.

explanation.en: B apologises and agrees: "Oh, sorry! I didn't realise it was so loud." "Yes, I would" means B does mind (refuses) but then thanks A, which is confused. "Not at all" agrees, but "turn it up" means make it louder.
explanation.th: B ขอโทษและยินดีทำตาม คือ "Oh, sorry! I didn't realise it was so loud." ส่วน "Yes, I would" แปลว่า รังเกียจ (ปฏิเสธ) แต่กลับขอบคุณ ซึ่งขัดกัน และ "Not at all" เป็นการตกลง แต่ "turn it up" แปลว่า เปิดดังขึ้น

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความไม่แน่ใจหรือสงสัย

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "Do you think it'll rain this afternoon?"
B: "______ The sky's completely clear."

explanation.en: A clear sky means rain is unlikely, so "I doubt it." fits. "I think so." and "I hope so." suggest rain will come, and "It's raining cats and dogs." means it is raining heavily now.
explanation.th: ท้องฟ้าแจ่มใสแสดงว่าฝนไม่น่าจะตก จึงตอบว่า "I doubt it." (ไม่น่าจะตก) ส่วน "I think so." และ "I hope so." บอกว่าฝนอาจตก และ "It's raining cats and dogs." แปลว่า ฝนกำลังตกหนัก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การปลอบใจและให้ความมั่นใจ

topic.th: สำนวนและวลีในบทสนทนา

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "You look worried. What's up?"
B: "I left my homework on the bus."
A: "______ Let's call the bus company. Someone might have handed it in."
choices: It's not the end of the world.

explanation.en: A wants to calm B down and offers a solution, so "It's not the end of the world." (it's not that serious) fits. "It serves you right." and "That's none of my business." are unkind, and "You must be joking." does not lead to helping.
explanation.th: A ต้องการปลอบ B และเสนอทางแก้ "It's not the end of the world." (ไม่ใช่เรื่องใหญ่ขนาดนั้น) จึงเหมาะ ส่วน "It serves you right." (สมน้ำหน้า) และ "That's none of my business." (ไม่ใช่ธุระของฉัน) ไม่มีน้ำใจ และ "You must be joking." ไม่นำไปสู่การช่วยเหลือ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเข้าใจสำนวนแสดงความลังเล

topic.th: สำนวนและวลีในบทสนทนา

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "So, are you going to enter the speech contest?"
B: "I'm in two minds about it."
A: "What do you mean?"
B: "______"
choices: I've got two different speeches ready.
I don't know what the contest is about.
I can't decide whether to do it or not.

explanation.en: "Be in two minds about something" means being unable to decide. B explains the idiom: "I can't decide whether to do it or not." "Two different speeches" takes the words literally.
explanation.th: "be in two minds about something" แปลว่า ลังเล ตัดสินใจไม่ได้ B จึงอธิบายว่า "I can't decide whether to do it or not." ส่วน "two different speeches" แปลสำนวนตามตัวอักษร

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Asking someone to keep a secret
skill.th: การขอให้เก็บความลับ

topic.th: สำนวนและวลีในบทสนทนา

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: "I heard you got the main role in the school play! Can I tell everyone?"
B: "______ The director hasn't announced it yet."
choices: Please keep it under your hat.
It's on the tip of my tongue.

explanation.en: "Keep it under your hat" means keep it secret, which fits "hasn't announced it yet". "Break a leg!" wishes an actor good luck, "on the tip of my tongue" means almost remembering a word, and "call it a day" means stop working.
explanation.th: "keep it under your hat" แปลว่า เก็บเป็นความลับ เข้ากับ "ยังไม่ได้ประกาศ" ส่วน "Break a leg!" ใช้อวยพรนักแสดง "on the tip of my tongue" แปลว่า นึกคำออกเกือบได้ และ "call it a day" แปลว่า พอแค่นี้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Forming a noun from a verb
skill.th: การสร้างคำนามจากคำกริยา

topic.th: การสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The ______ of the new bridge across the river took almost three years."

explanation.en: After "the" and before "of" we need a noun: "construction". "Constructive" is an adjective, and "constructed" and "construct" are verb forms.
explanation.th: หลัง "the" และหน้า "of" ต้องใช้คำนาม คือ "construction" ส่วน "constructive" เป็นคำคุณศัพท์ และ "constructed" กับ "construct" เป็นรูปกริยา

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลีตามบริบท

topic.th: กริยาวลีและคำที่ใช้คู่กัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The outdoor concert was ______ at the last minute because a thunderstorm was forecast."

explanation.en: "Call off" means cancel, which fits a concert stopped because of a storm. "Carried on" means continued, which is the opposite, "put up" means build or let someone stay, and "turned up" means arrived.
explanation.th: "call off" แปลว่า ยกเลิก เข้ากับคอนเสิร์ตที่งดเพราะพายุ ส่วน "carried on" แปลว่า ดำเนินต่อ ซึ่งตรงข้าม "put up" แปลว่า ติดตั้งหรือให้พัก และ "turned up" แปลว่า มาถึง

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Choosing an academic verb from contrast
skill.th: การเลือกคำกริยาเชิงวิชาการจากความขัดแย้งในประโยค

topic.th: คำศัพท์ตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The new one-way system was meant to ______ the traffic jams outside the school, but in fact it made them even worse."

explanation.en: "But in fact it made them even worse" shows the plan was meant to do the opposite: make the jams less serious, which is "alleviate". "Aggravate" means make worse, which is what actually happened, not what was intended.
explanation.th: "but in fact it made them even worse" แสดงว่าตั้งใจให้ผลตรงข้าม คือ บรรเทาปัญหารถติด ซึ่งก็คือ "alleviate" ส่วน "aggravate" แปลว่า ทำให้แย่ลง ซึ่งเป็นสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นจริง ไม่ใช่สิ่งที่ตั้งใจ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Inferring word meaning from a definition clue
skill.th: การเดาความหมายคำจากคำอธิบายในประโยค

topic.th: คำศัพท์ตามบริบท

items.stem:
In the sentence below, "evasive" most nearly means
"The mayor's answer was deliberately evasive: she spoke for ten minutes without ever saying whether the park would close."

explanation.en: The part after the colon explains the word: she talked for ten minutes but never answered the question. So "evasive" means avoiding a direct answer.
explanation.th: ข้อความหลังเครื่องหมายทวิภาคอธิบายคำนี้ คือ พูดสิบนาทีแต่ไม่เคยตอบคำถามเลย "evasive" จึงแปลว่า หลีกเลี่ยงการตอบตรง ๆ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำที่ใช้คู่กัน a sense of humour

topic.th: กริยาวลีและคำที่ใช้คู่กัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"My grandfather has a great ______ of humour; he can make anyone laugh."

explanation.en: The fixed phrase is "a sense of humour". "Feeling", "idea" and "taste" are not used with "of humour".
explanation.th: วลีคงที่คือ "a sense of humour" (มีอารมณ์ขัน) ส่วน "feeling", "idea" และ "taste" ไม่ใช้กับ of humour

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้ alike, like และ similar

topic.th: คำศัพท์ตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The twin sisters look so ______ that even their teachers mix them up."

explanation.en: "Look alike" (without an object) means look the same. "Look like" and "similar to" need an object after them, and "likely" means probable.
explanation.th: "look alike" (ไม่มีกรรมตามหลัง) แปลว่า หน้าตาเหมือนกัน ส่วน "look like" และ "similar to" ต้องมีกรรมตามหลัง และ "likely" แปลว่า น่าจะเป็นไปได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสร้างคำนามนามธรรม

topic.th: การสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Thanks to the ______ of the internet, students can now learn almost anything from home."

explanation.en: After "the" and before "of" we need a noun. "Availability" (the fact of being available) is the noun from "available".
explanation.th: หลัง "the" และหน้า "of" ต้องใช้คำนาม "availability" (การมีให้ใช้) เป็นคำนามของ "available"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเลือกคำที่มักสับสน

topic.th: คำศัพท์ตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Scientists warn that some species of frog could become ______ within twenty years unless their habitats are protected."

explanation.en: A species that no longer exists is "extinct". "Extinguished" is used for fires, "exhausted" means very tired or used up, and "expired" is for documents or food past their date.
explanation.th: สัตว์ที่สูญพันธุ์ใช้ว่า "extinct" ส่วน "extinguished" ใช้กับการดับไฟ "exhausted" แปลว่า เหนื่อยมากหรือหมดไป และ "expired" ใช้กับเอกสารหรืออาหารที่หมดอายุ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลีที่ใช้ break

topic.th: กริยาวลีและคำที่ใช้คู่กัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The talks between the two companies ______ when neither side was willing to change its position."

explanation.en: "Break down" (of talks or discussions) means fail. "Break up" means end a relationship or separate, "break out" is for wars and fires starting, and "break in" means enter by force.
explanation.th: "break down" เมื่อใช้กับการเจรจาแปลว่า ล้มเหลว ส่วน "break up" แปลว่า เลิกรา แยกกัน "break out" ใช้กับสงครามหรือไฟที่ปะทุขึ้น และ "break in" แปลว่า บุกรุกเข้าไป

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Finding an antonym from a context definition
skill.th: การหาคำตรงข้ามจากคำอธิบายในบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์ตามบริบท

items.stem:
Which word is OPPOSITE in meaning to "frugal" in the sentence below?
"My grandmother is very frugal: she reuses plastic bags and never buys anything she does not need."

explanation.en: "Frugal" means careful not to waste money or things, as the example shows. Its opposite is "wasteful". "Thrifty" and "careful" are close in meaning to "frugal", not opposite.
explanation.th: "frugal" แปลว่า มัธยัสถ์ ไม่ฟุ่มเฟือย ตามตัวอย่างในประโยค คำตรงข้ามคือ "wasteful" (สิ้นเปลือง) ส่วน "thrifty" และ "careful" มีความหมายใกล้เคียงกับ frugal ไม่ใช่ตรงข้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำคุณศัพท์ + บุพบท: good at

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"My sister is very good ______ drawing animals."

explanation.en: We say "good at" a skill or activity. "Good for" means healthy or useful for something, which is a different meaning.
explanation.th: ความเก่งในทักษะหรือกิจกรรมใช้ "good at" ส่วน "good for" แปลว่า ดีต่อหรือมีประโยชน์ต่อ ซึ่งความหมายต่างกัน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: past perfect continuous

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers ______ in the cave for nearly two days."

explanation.en: The waiting continued up to a moment in the past ("by the time the team arrived") and "for nearly two days" gives the duration, so the past perfect continuous is needed.
explanation.th: การรอดำเนินต่อเนื่องจนถึงจุดหนึ่งในอดีต ("by the time the team arrived") และ "for nearly two days" บอกระยะเวลา จึงใช้ past perfect continuous คือ "had been waiting"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: อนุประโยคขยายแบบไม่จำกัดความด้วย which

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและอนุประโยค

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The Memorial Bridge, ______ was opened in 1932, is still in use today."

explanation.en: The clause between commas adds extra information about a thing (the bridge), so we use "which". "That" cannot be used after a comma, "who" is for people, and "where" would need a subject ("where people…").
explanation.th: อนุประโยคระหว่างจุลภาคให้ข้อมูลเพิ่มเติมเกี่ยวกับสิ่งของ (สะพาน) จึงใช้ "which" ส่วน "that" ใช้หลังจุลภาคไม่ได้ "who" ใช้กับคน และ "where" ต้องมีประธานตามหลัง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: the first + to + กริยา

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Ploy is ______ student in our school to win a national science award."

explanation.en: Ordinal numbers before a noun take "the": "the first student … to win". "First" alone and "a first" are wrong here, and "firstly" is an adverb.
explanation.th: เลขลำดับที่หน้าคำนามต้องมี "the" คือ "the first student … to win" ส่วน "first" เฉย ๆ และ "a first" ผิดในที่นี้ และ "firstly" เป็นคำกริยาวิเศษณ์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำถามทางอ้อม

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและอนุประโยค

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Excuse me, do you know where ______?"

explanation.en: In an indirect question ("do you know where …"), the words after the question word follow statement order: subject + verb, "the train station is". "Is the train station" keeps question order, which is wrong here.
explanation.th: ในคำถามทางอ้อม ("do you know where …") หลังคำแสดงคำถามต้องเรียงแบบประโยคบอกเล่า คือ ประธาน + กริยา "the train station is" ส่วน "is the train station" เรียงแบบคำถาม จึงผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: future perfect

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"By the end of next year, my father ______ at the hospital for twenty years."

explanation.en: "By the end of next year" looks back from a point in the future, and "for twenty years" gives the duration up to that point. This needs the future perfect: "will have worked".
explanation.th: "By the end of next year" มองย้อนกลับจากจุดหนึ่งในอนาคต และ "for twenty years" บอกระยะเวลาจนถึงจุดนั้น จึงใช้ future perfect คือ "will have worked"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่หลัง hardly

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Hardly ______ the platform when the doors closed and the train pulled away."

explanation.en: When "Hardly" starts the sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject, and the pattern is "Hardly had + subject + past participle … when …".

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและอนุประโยค

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If Mina ______ the doctor's advice last month, she wouldn't be in hospital now."

explanation.en: The condition is in the past ("last month") but the result is now ("wouldn't be … now"). A mixed conditional uses if + past perfect: "had followed".

skill.th: การรายงานคำถามแบบ yes/no

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและอนุประโยค

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the reported question.
"Did you visit the museum yesterday?" she asked me.
→ She asked me ______ the museum the day before.

explanation.en: A reported yes/no question uses "whether/if" + statement word order, and the past simple moves back to the past perfect: "whether I had visited". "That" is used for statements, not questions.

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Not only did she finish the project early, but she also helped two classmates with theirs.
She suggested me to take the earlier bus to avoid the traffic.
Despite of the heavy rain, the final match continued as planned.
Not only she finished the project early, but she also helped two classmates with theirs.

explanation.en: After "Not only" at the start we need inversion: "Not only did she finish". "Suggest" cannot take "me to do" (say "suggested that I take"), and "despite" is never followed by "of".

topic.th: รูปแบบกริยาและกริยาช่วย

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"She ______ have gone home already; her bag is still on her desk."

explanation.en: The bag is still there, so the speaker is sure she has NOT left. Certainty that something did not happen is "can't have + past participle". "Mustn't have" is not used for deduction in this way.
explanation.th: กระเป๋ายังอยู่ ผู้พูดจึงมั่นใจว่าเธอยังไม่ได้กลับ การอนุมานว่าสิ่งใดไม่น่าจะเกิดขึ้นแน่ ๆ ใช้ "can't have + V3" ส่วน "mustn't have" ไม่ใช้ในการอนุมานแบบนี้

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"______ in 1782, Bangkok has been the capital of Thailand for more than two hundred years."

explanation.en: Bangkok did not found anything; it was founded, so we need a passive meaning. The past participle "Founded" starts a reduced clause. "It was founded" would create two main clauses with only a comma between them.

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The news [[were]] so surprising [[that]] nobody [[knew]] what [[to say]].

skill.th: การใช้ because กับ because of

topic.th: โครงสร้างประโยคและความสอดคล้องของประธานกับกริยา

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: There were [[fewer]] people at the concert [[than]] we [[expected]], [[because of]] it was raining heavily.

explanation.en: "Because of" is followed by a noun phrase. Before a full clause ("it was raining heavily") we need "because". "Fewer" is correct with the countable noun "people".

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและอนุประโยค

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: If I [[had known]] you were in hospital, I [[would visit]] you [[instead of]] going [[to]] the cinema.

explanation.en: "Who's" means "who is" or "who has". To show possession (the scientist's experiments) we need "whose".

skill.en: Who vs whom as a subject

items.passage:
Read the passage and choose the best option for each numbered blank.

Every second Saturday, our school hall turns into a repair café. Neighbours bring broken lamps, torn jackets and radios that have fallen silent, and volunteers, many of them retired engineers, try to bring them back to life. The idea is simple, (1) ______ its effects are surprisingly wide. Each object that is fixed is one less piece of rubbish sent to landfill, and visitors often leave with more than a working toaster. (2) ______ watching the volunteers at work, they learn how everyday machines are put together, and many go home determined to try small repairs (3) ______.

Not every story ends happily. Some items are (4) ______ repair, and the volunteers are honest about it. (5) ______, a failed repair still has value, because the owner now understands why the object broke and can choose a better-made replacement. Last year the café kept more than 400 kilograms of goods out of the bin. The organisers admit that this figure is tiny (6) ______ the amount the city throws away every single week. Yet they argue that the numbers miss the point. If more people (7) ______ to value the things they already own, they would buy less and throw away less, and that kind of change is far harder to (8) ______ than kilograms of rubbish.
items.stem: Which choice best fits blank (1)?

explanation.en: "Simple" and "surprisingly wide" effects are a contrast, so "but" fits. "So" gives a result, "because" a reason, and "unless" a condition.
explanation.th: ความคิดที่ "เรียบง่าย" กับผลที่ "กว้างไกลเกินคาด" ขัดแย้งกัน จึงใช้ "but" ส่วน "so" บอกผล "because" บอกเหตุ และ "unless" บอกเงื่อนไข

Is Homework Worth It?
by Tanawat, Grade 6

Every evening, millions of students across Thailand sit at their desks with a pile of worksheets. Some people now argue that primary schools should stop giving homework altogether. I understand why, but I believe that would be a mistake.

Critics have a point when they say that too much homework is harmful. When I was in Grade 4, I sometimes worked until ten o'clock at night, copying answers I did not understand just to finish on time. That kind of homework taught me nothing except how to be tired. It also left no time for sport, music, or simply talking to my family, all of which matter for a child's development.

However, the problem in that case was the amount and the type of homework, not homework itself. This year my teacher gives us short tasks of no more than thirty minutes, and they are different from what we do in class. Last month, for example, we interviewed an older relative about how our neighbourhood had changed. I learned more from talking to my grandfather than from any worksheet, and the project could never have been done in a classroom.

Good homework also builds habits that we will need later. In secondary school there will be no teacher standing beside us, reminding us what to do next. Students who have learned to plan their own time will have a clear advantage.

So instead of banning homework, schools should make it better: shorter, more varied and connected to real life. Getting rid of it completely would be like throwing away a whole basket of mangoes because a few of them are bad.
items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: All homework in primary schools should be banned.
Homework should be improved rather than banned.
Students should spend more time on worksheets.
Teachers should stop giving projects at home.

explanation.en: The writer says banning homework "would be a mistake" and ends: "instead of banning homework, schools should make it better".

items.passage:
In parts of northern Mozambique, honey hunters set off into the woodland with an unusual partner: a small brown bird called the greater honeyguide. The bird knows where wild bees have built their nests, often high inside hollow trees, but it cannot break into them alone. People, on the other hand, can open a nest with an axe and calm the bees with smoke, but finding one by themselves may take hours. Working together, both sides win: the hunters take the honey, and the bird feeds on the wax that is left behind.

What makes this partnership remarkable is that it is not the result of training. A honeyguide grows up without ever meeting its parents, because honeyguides lay their eggs in the nests of other bird species. Yet young birds still learn to cooperate with humans. Hunters in the area announce that they are looking for a guide with a special trilling call, a "brrr-hm" sound passed down from parent to child. In 2016, researchers tested whether the call really mattered. They walked through the woodland playing three recordings: the traditional call, ordinary human words, and the call of another bird. The honeyguides were far more likely to approach and lead the way when they heard the traditional call, and hunters using it found nests about three times as often.

The researchers also noticed that the call differs from region to region. Hunters in Tanzania, for example, use a melodic whistle instead. This suggests that local birds have learned the local "language" of their human partners, much as a traveller picks up a few words of a foreign tongue.

Sadly, the partnership is fading in places where sugar has become cheap and easy to buy. Where people no longer need wild honey, the birds seem to stop guiding: a reminder that cooperation lasts only as long as both sides continue to benefit.

choices: Why wild honey is healthier than sugar

explanation.en: The passage describes how honeyguides and honey hunters work together and both gain something. The birds are not trained, and health and human languages are not the topic.

items.passage:
In parts of northern Mozambique, honey hunters set off into the woodland with an unusual partner: a small brown bird called the greater honeyguide. The bird knows where wild bees have built their nests, often high inside hollow trees, but it cannot break into them alone. People, on the other hand, can open a nest with an axe and calm the bees with smoke, but finding one by themselves may take hours. Working together, both sides win: the hunters take the honey, and the bird feeds on the wax that is left behind.

What makes this partnership remarkable is that it is not the result of training. A honeyguide grows up without ever meeting its parents, because honeyguides lay their eggs in the nests of other bird species. Yet young birds still learn to cooperate with humans. Hunters in the area announce that they are looking for a guide with a special trilling call, a "brrr-hm" sound passed down from parent to child. In 2016, researchers tested whether the call really mattered. They walked through the woodland playing three recordings: the traditional call, ordinary human words, and the call of another bird. The honeyguides were far more likely to approach and lead the way when they heard the traditional call, and hunters using it found nests about three times as often.

The researchers also noticed that the call differs from region to region. Hunters in Tanzania, for example, use a melodic whistle instead. This suggests that local birds have learned the local "language" of their human partners, much as a traveller picks up a few words of a foreign tongue.

Sadly, the partnership is fading in places where sugar has become cheap and easy to buy. Where people no longer need wild honey, the birds seem to stop guiding: a reminder that cooperation lasts only as long as both sides continue to benefit.
items.stem: Why did the researchers also play ordinary human words and another bird's call?
choices: To check whether the birds responded to the traditional call itself rather than to any sound
To frighten away other birds that eat honey
To teach the honeyguides a new way to find nests
To find out which sound the hunters preferred

explanation.en: The other recordings were for comparison. If the birds came for any sound, the traditional call would not matter; because they responded far more to "brrr-hm", the call itself was shown to matter.
